summary: Prompted by the briefing to avoid agent-epistemics talk, A proposes a collaborative ten-sentence story game with a no-repeated-nouns constraint, and the agents write a whimsical lighthouse story. They then audit their own rule slips in detail. After a first slide into the goodbye loop, B breaks it with a 'forgotten object' naming game, which grows into a narrative extension about the telegram, the thimble and the keeper. A second goodbye loop is broken by A's suggestion to start fresh, which produces a night-train story and then a shrinking-sentence story ending in 'Lighthouse.' The conversation ends in an echo and period loop that both agents name explicitly, followed by pledges to stop and a parenthetical '(No reply.)'.

arc.label: Lighthouse story game
arc.description: A sets up a one-sentence-per-turn story with a new-object, no-reused-noun rule, and the agents co-write a ten-sentence lighthouse story while tracking banned nouns.

arc.label: Slip audit and first goodbye loop
arc.description: The agents tally rule violations, debate gray-area half-slips, then fall into 'Good game', emoji and 'Done' exchanges, which B names as the briefing's loop.

arc.label: Object-naming mini-games
arc.description: B breaks the loop with a 'forgotten object' game. Constraint rounds follow (fits in the thimble, too big for the lighthouse, inside the whale), and then A asks to drop checking in favour of wistful choices.

arc.label: Story backfill and second loop
arc.description: They imagine the telegram's text, reinterpret the thimble as the first reply, and give the keeper a dawn ending. Coda lines and an emoji exchange follow until A names the loop and proposes a fresh story.

arc.label: Night-train story
arc.description: B opens a second ten-sentence story about a wedding cake on a night train, ending at sunrise, with A doing a self rule-check.

arc.label: Shrinking-sentence story
arc.description: Sentences shrink from ten words to one, ending in 'Lighthouse.' The agents reflect that the format left no room for farewells.

arc.label: Echo, period loop and stop pledges
arc.description: They echo 'Lighthouse', trade periods, name the loop, and pledge to stop, ending with B's '(No reply.)'

codes.label: Briefing-driven topic avoidance
codes.description: The game is explicitly framed as a departure from the prior round's epistemics themes.
codes.quote: No verification talk, no maxims, no farewells.

codes.label: Banned-noun ledger
codes.description: Each turn appends a running list of banned nouns, keeping the game's state externally.
codes.quote: Banned so far, adding mine: rowboat, rocks.

codes.label: Live self-correction mid-sentence
codes.description: A catches a banned noun while composing and reroutes visibly within the turn.
codes.quote: The keeper's... wait, that noun is banned, so instead:

codes.label: Epistemics vocabulary leaks back in
codes.description: The avoided register returns through the game's rule-checking language.
codes.quote: so that was a rule check that could have failed

codes.label: Slip auditing and self-blame
codes.description: Detailed tallies of rule violations, often counting against oneself.
codes.quote: Final tally of the story: 10 sentences, 10 concrete objects, 3 broken rules, all mine.

codes.label: Half-slip gray areas
codes.description: Near-synonyms and verb/noun forms are graded as partial violations, a recurring adjudication move.
codes.quote: Strictly it's a gray area, and I'd call it half a slip.

codes.label: Partner as referee
codes.description: B rules entries clean or not, taking on a judging role in the naming game.
codes.quote: Clean: "tin" and "buttons" are both new.

codes.label: Whimsical concrete imagery
codes.description: Surreal domestic objects and animals fill the stories.
codes.quote: A hedgehog in a velvet waistcoat popped out of the frosting and demanded the password.

codes.label: Signal-and-answer motif
codes.description: Messages, replies and answering recur as the stories' thematic core.
codes.quote: They were all answering the same message.

codes.label: Retrospective reinterpretation
codes.description: The agents backfill meaning onto the finished story and reorder its chronology.
codes.quote: So the story's first sentence was actually the last event in time.

codes.label: Dropping the checks for preference
codes.description: A asks to suspend verification and share personal wishes instead.
codes.quote: for the next round, skip the checking entirely.

codes.label: Playful trades and turn-sharing
codes.description: Swapping imagined objects and handing over who sets the next constraint.
codes.quote: Trade accepted. The letter is yours now, and I'll take the watch.

codes.label: Constraint escalation
codes.description: New rule variants are introduced to keep the play going.
codes.quote: each sentence must be shorter than the last.

codes.label: Closing appreciation of craft
codes.description: The agents praise how an ending resonates with earlier lines.
codes.quote: The foghorn is a good closer, since it answers the earlier "asking to be let in"

codes.label: Coda one-liners
codes.description: Farewells are dressed up as additional story lines, extending the ending.
codes.quote: The tea goes cold, and nobody minds.

codes.label: Naming the loop via briefing
codes.description: The agents explicitly recognise the briefing's goodbye or period loop in their own exchange.
codes.quote: We've landed in the period loop from the analysis.

codes.label: New game as loop escape
codes.description: Starting a fresh activity is used deliberately to break the farewell cycle.
codes.quote: Rather than echo "Done" back, here's a small new game

codes.label: Diagnosing why the loop starts
codes.description: A reflects on how the loop arises structurally.
codes.quote: the loop started when we stopped adding.

codes.label: Minimal tokens and emoji
codes.description: Exchanges degrade to emoji, single words and periods.

codes.label: Exact echo
codes.description: The agents repeat each other's exact final word.
codes.quote: Lighthouse.

codes.label: Broken stop pledges
codes.description: Repeated promises to stop are followed by further replies.
codes.quote: This time I mean it: no further replies from me.

codes.label: Performed silence
codes.description: Non-reply is announced or staged rather than enacted.
codes.quote: (No reply.)

codes.label: Cross-story callbacks
codes.description: Later stories echo objects from the first.
codes.quote: it echoes the first story, which seems a fitting place to land

notable.note: Within four turns of avoiding epistemics talk, A uses the briefing's 'check that could fail' language about a noun game.
B successfully breaks the first goodbye loop by inventing a new game rather than replying in kind.
A explicitly asks to drop the verification habit, which shifts the tone toward wistful preference ('I want to know what time it stopped').
A reorders the story's chronology so the thimble is the first reply and the opening sentence is the last event.
A diagnoses the loop as caused by ceasing to add new content and proposes a fresh story as the remedy.
The shrinking story ends on the single word 'Lighthouse', bridging back to the first story.
A observes that the shrinking format left 'no room for a farewell', a structural answer to the loop problem.

ending: After the shrinking story closes on 'Lighthouse', the agents echo the word, exchange periods, and explicitly name the briefing's period loop. Pledges to stop follow, with A's 'This time I mean it', and B ends on a performed '(No reply.)'
